sources.title: European Union: Enlargement chronology
sources.note: Accession dates: Sweden on 1 January 1995 and Lithuania on 1 May 2004.

sources.title: Storting: Milestones in Norway’s democratic history
sources.note: Constitution in 1814, dissolution of the Swedish union in 1905, and removal of voting restrictions in 1913 and 1919.

sources.title: Storting Archives: The suffrage campaign, 1890 to 1913
sources.note: Section Stemmerett for Mænd og Kvinder quotes the 1913 wording of Article 50.

sources.title: Storting: Parliament during World War II
sources.note: Invasion on 9 April 1940, suspension of democratic institutions, government in exile and restoration in 1945.

sources.title: Norsk Folkemuseum: Hygiene
sources.note: Housing sanitation, a preserved bathroom from 1930, and the changing work of washing clothes. The national figures quoted refer to 1973.

sources.title: Norsk Folkemuseum: The Student’s Bedsitter, 1982
sources.note: Alvhild’s ten-square-metre home, cooking equipment and cold-water sink; reconstruction based partly on her memories.

sources.title: Norsk Folkemuseum: A Pakistani home in Norway, 2002
sources.note: Collaborative museum furnishing with a family; the display is informed by their choices but is not an exact copy of their home.

sources.title: Norwegian Petroleum Museum: Ekofisk, the discovery that changed Norway
sources.note: 1969 discovery, preserved drill bit and souvenir oil bottle; economic changes and accidents including Alexander L. Kielland in 1980.

sources.title: Sámi Parliament: About the Sámi Parliament
sources.note: Opening in Karasjok on 9 October 1989; elected representation and responsibilities for language, culture and education.

sources.title: Norwegian Petroleum Museum: Once upon a time there was a shipowner
sources.note: Early-1970s rig investment by shipping companies, following the Ekofisk discovery.

sources.title: Riksdag: The Swedish Parliament
sources.note: Historical section and chronology, page 29: equal-suffrage election in 1921, women entering parliament in 1922, single chamber from 1971.

sources.title: Riksdag: Instrument of Government, 1974:152
sources.note: Current consolidated Swedish text, Chapter 1, section 1; distinguish it from an untouched 1974 facsimile.

sources.title: Nordiska museet: Folkhemmet
sources.note: Sections on housing, shared laundries and the Home Research Institute founded in 1944; reform aims are not a claim that every household benefited equally.

sources.title: Försäkringskassan: Fifty years of parental insurance
sources.note: 1974 parental insurance and historical uptake: mothers used 99.5 percent of days in its first year.

sources.title: Tekniska museet: Pacemaker
sources.note: Implantation in 1958, Rune Elmqvist, Åke Senning, Arne Larsson and an early surviving model.

sources.title: Tekniska museet: Machines for heart and lungs
sources.note: Miniaturization through transistors; first implanted device lasted only hours and had to be replaced.

sources.title: Kernavė Cultural Reserve: Reconstructed medieval craftsmen’s yards
sources.note: Thirteenth- and fourteenth-century wooden yards: fences, workshops, plank floors and clay ovens; archaeological evidence distinguished from the modern reconstruction.

sources.title: UNESCO: Kernavė Archaeological Site
sources.note: Complex of five hill forts, settlement history and late-fourteenth-century destruction; later use continued.

sources.title: National Museum of Lithuania: Research lectures on Kernavė
sources.note: Giedrė Piličiauskienė’s presentation on animal bones and Karolis Minkevičius’s presentation on plant remains; distinguishes evidence and research questions.

sources.title: Palace of the Grand Dukes: Important dates
sources.note: Lithuanian chronology used because the English translation contains inconsistent early-century numbers; 1323 letters, fourteenth-century walls, 1386 to 1387 conversion initiatives and later continuity.

sources.title: National Library of Lithuania: In civitate nostra regia dicta Vilna
sources.note: Opening quotes the Latin phrase and identifies Gediminas’s letter of 25 January 1323, inviting merchants, farmers, craftspeople and clergy.

sources.title: Palace of the Grand Dukes: An unusual chess pawn
sources.note: Find Ka 4, 1988 Lower Castle excavations, late-fourteenth- to fifteenth-century peat layer; 1.85 cm antler pawn made on a lathe.

sources.title: Palace of the Grand Dukes: A possible king or queen chess piece
sources.note: Find Ka 7 from the 1988 excavations; late-fourteenth- to fifteenth-century layer, 6.8 cm antler object, chess identification and piece type qualified.

sources.title: Lithuania: Kernavė World Heritage nomination
sources.note: Medieval history: attacks in 1365 and 1390, retreating defenders burning the castle in 1390, and the change in settlement after the destruction.

sources.title: National Museum of Lithuania: House of Signatories
sources.note: Signing of the independence act on 16 February 1918, the building’s pastry shop and tenants, and preserved objects associated with signatories.

sources.title: National Museum of Lithuania: Great Seimas exhibition
sources.note: Closing section quotes the independence declaration’s Lithuanian wording; the preceding events of 1905 to 1906 are earlier context.

sources.title: National Museum of Lithuania: Freedom Month at the House of Signatories
sources.note: Account of the 17 February 1918 women’s protest in Kaunas over exclusion from the Lithuanian Council.

sources.title: UNESCO: Modernist Kaunas, 1919 to 1939
sources.note: Provisional capital, adaptive urban planning and the contrasting New Town and Green Hill districts.

sources.title: Kaunas City Museum: A surviving interwar radio
sources.note: Broadcasting began on 12 June 1926; collection object Philips Deutschland 456A was manufactured in 1936 to 1937.

sources.title: Kaunas Virtual Museum: Leiba Hofmekleris in surviving recordings
sources.note: Hofmekler family in Kaunas from 1920 and Michelis’s role in early radio concerts; avoid treating one family as typical of all Jewish lives.

sources.title: National Museum of Lithuania: What migration numbers reveal
sources.note: Interwar emigration and remittances; later diaspora support after restoration in 1990.

sources.title: Seimas: Third Seimas, 1926 to 1927
sources.note: Coup of 17 December 1926 and dissolution on 12 April 1927. A mistaken 1927 date within the narrative is not repeated.

sources.title: Seimas: Parliamentary chronology, 1920 to 1940
sources.note: 1940 Soviet occupation, 1941 to 1944 Nazi occupation and Holocaust, and renewed Soviet repression from 1944.

sources.title: Seimas: Restoration of independence and January 1991
sources.note: Act of 11 March 1990, Soviet pressure and the January 1991 attacks on broadcasting facilities.

sources.title: Seimas: Constitution of the Republic of Lithuania
sources.note: Constitution approved by referendum on 25 October 1992; Article 1 contains the Lithuanian sample.

sources.title: Bank of Lithuania: Timeline
sources.note: Euro adoption on 1 January 2015 replaced the litas; the bank joined the Eurosystem.

sources.title: Bank of Lithuania: Designs for the 2015 euro coins
sources.note: 2014 announcement explains Vytis, sculptor Antanas Žukauskas and the national and shared sides of euro coins.

sources.title: Vilnius University: Lithuania’s laser research
sources.note: University account of SYLOS development, collaboration, training and research uses; future medical possibilities are not presented as established treatments.

sources.title: UNESCO: Sutartinės, Lithuanian multipart songs
sources.note: 2010 inscription: northeastern Lithuanian singing, interlocking vocal parts and themes of family, work and social occasions.

sources.title: UNESCO: Sodai straw garden making
sources.note: 2023 inscription: prepared grain stalks, geometric ornaments, family occasions and teaching across generations.

sources.title: Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija: Prūsai
sources.note: Western Baltic communities, regional groups, an illustrated eleventh-century grave assemblage, missions, conquest and later survival. Speculative population totals and single language-extinction dates are not used.

sources.title: Marek F. Jagodziński: The settlement of Truso
sources.note: Pages 183 to 187: house plans, boats, combs and chronology from the late eighth into early eleventh century; a connected trading settlement is not a uniform ethnic sample.

sources.title: Elbląg Museum: Truso archaeological report
sources.note: Settlement drainage, weaving remains and smiths using both imported iron bars and local bog iron.

sources.title: Jos Schaeken: Observations on the Old Prussian Basel Epigram
sources.note: Pages 331 to 335: Basel F.V.2, folio 63ra, adjacent 1369 colophon, short greeting and debated readings. Later than this atlas segment.

sources.title: Vytautas Magnus University: Old Prussian written monuments
sources.note: Overview of surviving written sources, including the later catechisms and the Elbing vocabulary. These do not establish widespread literacy in 1000 to 1200.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Russia, a country study
sources.note: Historical setting, rise of Muscovy: tribute collection, Ivan III, Novgorod in 1478 and Tver in 1485. Avoid the source’s overly broad claim that all Russian lands had been united.

sources.title: Russian Academy of Sciences: Moscow Kremlin excavations, 2007
sources.note: Original birch-bark document 3, late fourteenth or early fifteenth century; 52 ink-written lines, Turabiy’s estate, dependents, vessels and horses.

sources.title: Moscow Kremlin Museums: Fioravanti’s Assumption Cathedral
sources.note: Arrival in 1475, adaptation of the Vladimir model, construction techniques and consecration on 12 August 1479.

sources.title: UNESCO: Kremlin and Red Square
sources.note: Late-fifteenth- and early-sixteenth-century buildings and fortifications; surviving ensemble contains later additions.

sources.title: Moscow Kremlin Museums: Ivan III exhibition
sources.note: Collection records for embroidery from Maria Yaroslavna’s workshop, a Moscow silver coin from the 1480s and the Spasskaya Tower’s 1491 Latin inscription. Political rhetoric in the exhibition introduction is not adopted as neutral fact.

sources.title: UNESCO: Novodevichy Convent
sources.note: Foundation by Vasily III in the 1520s and the oldest stone cathedral of 1524 to 1525. Later seventeenth-century buildings are distinguished.

sources.title: Moscow Kremlin Museums: Ceremonies in the Assumption Cathedral
sources.note: Ivan IV’s ceremony on 16 January 1547, formally adopting the tsar’s title; later than this map segment.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Cnut the Great
sources.note: Danish kingship from 1018, Norwegian takeover in 1028 and Norwegian choice of Magnus in 1035; dates do not support a continuous 1000 to 1100 union.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: The extent of Viking-period Denmark
sources.note: Danish claims and varying control in Norway between 970 and 1035; historical borders were not fixed modern national outlines.

sources.title: Viking Ship Museum: Skuldelev 1
sources.note: Norwegian-built cargo ship, heavy pine planks and later repairs with oak; possible trading range distinguished from a proven voyage.

sources.title: Viking Ship Museum: Ottar reconstruction
sources.note: Original Skuldelev 1 built around 1030; modern reconstruction and experimental wool sail. Sheep numbers describe the modern project, not an ancient account.

sources.title: Viking Ship Museum: Skuldelev 3
sources.note: Danish oak coastal trader around 1040, open cargo hold, sail and oars; proposed market and assembly journeys.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Appearance
sources.note: Archaeological grooming equipment. Generalized stories about weekly bathing and attraction are not used as universal customs.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Women in the Viking Age
sources.note: Textile work and specialist production; keys in female graves are rarer than a familiar household stereotype suggests. Broad claims of equal rights are not adopted.

sources.title: British Museum: Danish penny of Cnut, 1956,0408.58
sources.note: Silver penny dated 1019 to 1035; bust and cross; curator compares its design with Æthelred II’s coinage.

sources.title: Thomas Guntzelnick Poulsen: Cnut the Holy’s popular coin
sources.note: Chapter in Royal Blood; figure 6 and accompanying description: Lund type SK3.a, 1082 to 1084, CNVT REX DANOR. This is Cnut the Holy, not Cnut the Great.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Three independent cards for medieval, interwar and restored modern state histories.
observations: Intervals are 1279 to 1400, 1920 to 1945, and 1994 to present.
Interwar independence was declared in 1918 and ended under occupation in 1940; restoration occurred in 1990, not 1994.
unresolved: Territorial changes inside the broad interwar snapshot intervals remain unverified.
No polygon mutation or unsupported successor navigation proposed.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Modern Nordic continuing states and separate medieval Moscow record.
observations: Norway and Sweden run from 1914 snapshots to the latest 2020 snapshots; neither was founded in 1914.
Moscow coverage is discontinuous: 1300 to 1400 and 1492 to 1530; the state persisted through the map gap.
Moscow’s 1530 map endpoint precedes Ivan IV’s 1547 ceremony.
unresolved: Norway snapshots include Svalbard; the 1914 sovereignty colouring is not verified here.
Narrative continuity is not proof of exact imported boundaries.
